findings.title: per-atom gate can be diluted by filler atoms
findings.change: perf_budget.py votes on bytes per *unique validated obligation* rather than per raw atom; adds scale profiles at 2/237/801 atoms, a single very long clause probe, a padding-invariance probe, and separates disk/serialized bytes from model-context bytes (declared uncomputable without a bound tokenizer instead of being invented). Independent challenge C4 then defeated the first denominator by re-stamping filler atoms with fresh subject_id/req_id; the round repaired that on 2026-10-10 - the denominator is now CONTENT-addressed (sha256 of the atom's normalised statement), an atom that asserts nothing is accounted as unvalidated_atom_count and can never vote, and the rejected identity-addressed count plus the rate it would have produced are printed beside the vote.
evidence: tools/perf_budget.py --check -> exit 0, verdict PASS, voting_row bytes_per_atom, denominator unique_obligations (evidence/perf_budget_check.json)
padding probe: 1 unique obligation / 7492 B per obligation before -> 501 atoms but still 1 unique obligation / 42492 B per obligation after; padding cannot push the row under budget
recorded historical row preserved verbatim and visible: context_bytes_per_artefact 343547 > 20000 budget, recorded=true, verdict FAIL, exceeded=true
tests/test_perf_budget.py extended; UAT-11 (source+install) PASS with s2_preserved_fail_visible=True

independent challenge C4 attack, now measured in the tool's own output: identical filler -> 1 unique obligation / 42492 B per obligation; re-stamped-id filler -> still 1 unique obligation / 49492 B per obligation, while the rejected identity-addressed denominator would have reported 98.79 B per obligation (below the 2000 budget) - i.e. the attack that passed before now fails, and its success under the old rule stays visible (evidence/perf_budget_check_after_c4.json)
tests/test_perf_budget.py: test_restamped_ids_do_not_create_obligations, test_an_atom_without_a_statement_is_not_an_obligation, test_restamped_filler_ids_also_fail_to_dilute; 29 tests OK
live measurement unchanged where it should be: 237 unique obligations, 1449.6 B per obligation, verdict PASS (the real PI's 237 atoms are 237 genuinely distinct statements)
findings.residual: Scope of the claim: the rule resists filler and identity re-stamping. A payload whose filler asserts genuinely DISTINCT statements is, by construction, a payload with distinct obligations and is judged as such - it also pays bytes for each one. The 2000 B budget and PER_ATOM_BYTES(2000) owner ruling are unchanged.

findings.observation: A3: when the *authorised root itself* is a symlink, the tool resolves it and publishes into its real target. That is self-consistent (the destination's real path stays inside the real path of the authorised root) and no victim was touched, but the tool does not warn that the authorised root is a symlink. Classified ORACLE_DISAGREEMENT for the owner: either document it as accepted behaviour or refuse symlinked authorised roots.
